data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:65 | [2025-03-07 19:15] derbymanager : - Fixed the gk market, bots will now sometimes sell if they have 3 or more. - When failing to receive the ball after a pass it won't automatically go to the defender. It will rebound and the closest player (maybe even the same one) will pick it up. This is the same as it works when attempting a pass, the defender doesn't automatically gain possession. In all other non pass-related tackles the defender gains possession.  Since a pass consists of 2 steps, passing and receiving, that's two chances for failure with each pass while all other actions have only one. And succeeding 2x is harder than succeeding 1x. So now each failure has a chance to, uhm, fail and undo the failure making it a success of some kind 🙂 This should make actions deadlier and last longer...

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:82 | [2025-06-02 19:00] derbymanager : - You can now pay off any missing money to upgrade facilities (the limit was previously at 1M and then at 2.5M). The board will still only allow upgrades up to few levels above their target (e.g. if your facilities are at 22 and target is at 16 you maybe won't be able to pay for upgrades. - There is a new spider graph for players, always visible, so <@439665894021398539> and everyone can get a better/faster overview of opponent players. The graph gives out the average value of 3 related skills and is useful to quickly make sense of what kind of player one is.  ---  *Anyway, I'll try to explain again how facilities work. Think of them as being a bank.  1. You put money into them (effectively losing it for transfers). This happens when the investment is above 100%. 2. The money in the bank gives you revenue from interest (in our case it's better training, higher salary cap, etc...). 3. You can take the money out of the bank, losing some of the interest revenue (benefits). This happens under 100% investment.  Your board aims to keep finances stable. If you don't earn money, they won't invest. If you're earning too much, they'll invest a part of it. If you're behind too much they'll invest more, if you're close to the target they'll invest less. If you want to overinvest, you have to do it yourself by earning money and manually putting it into facilities.  Allowing you to put 10M directly into the bank instead of waiting for X weeks for that to happen effectively changes only the time variable. Financially it is the same. You also get benefits from that investment but lose cash for players. And, in the end, if you can't support that level your board will lower investment below 100% and you'll get your money back (slowly over time). It's literally like moving money from one bucket (cash) to another (facilities).  Hope that helps.*

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:93 | [2025-07-26 07:14] derbymanager : **Announcement for s14**  Oldies right now get certain boosts in the match engine but those are not shown anywhere and most managers are unaware of them. A lot of people (probably the vast majority)  therefore expect the same results from a 3 star youngster and a 3 star oldie on the pitch and might get frustrated that their young squad underperforms. So for the next season I will change how match modifiers work (sharpness, form...) and will represent them with a single icon that should tell you what to expect from each player in a match (e.g. for each player you'll know that this player will likely get yellow or blue face if you play him or whatever). In addition, I'll improve and explicitly show the boost oldies get from experience to showcase that these players are worth to keep.  The general concept doesn't change much. Youngsters vary in their performance. They can play great one game and bad the next one, while oldies give consistently good output on the pitch. This is, more or less, how it works now but it isn't obvious. I'll emphasize that a bit more both visually and in the code.  TL;DR. You need oldies both for training and results.  ps. oldies are 30+ but age is just one part of it and experience and skills play their part of course. Youngsters improve in price and can bring you money, oldies lose value but improve others and can bring you results. You need a healthy mixture of both.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:3472 | [2023-07-10 10:21] derbymanager : Just thinking out loud:  - work rate can be trained even above the natural limit but if you stop training it it'll drop back down. Training physical skills is also the smallest training (will only be the 3 physical skills). It grows a bit faster, when possible due to age. - determination grows slowly if trained, otherwise it stays static. It is recalculated (randomised based on xp) after a transfer. There is also a chance to recalculate it between seasons (or windows), higher chance for players that won a trophy (again, based on xp as well). - focus can be trained a bit faster but it can also drop at any time due to random events.

Focus - ME: passing actions + penalties + fouls + offsides and other small "mistakes" - non ME: affects satisfaction (i.e. the player is partying and it hurts team spirit) - Behaves: grows faster when trained, drops faster when not playing, drops slowly when not training (depends on xp-pressure)  Determination - ME: saves and shots,  - non ME: fewer skill drops (determined players last longer, which is often the case for gks and forwards), a bit better training - Behaves: chance to change during transfer windows, will certainly change when changing clubs (depending on xp-adaptability)  Work rate - ME: movement actions, can "refuse" to move into position if he's tired - non ME: affects the condition loss and fitness indirectly - Behaves: can be trained above the natural tendency but it'll drop back when training stops, depends on age and xp-professionalism

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:3549 | [2023-07-10 21:14] derbymanager : Right now values are assigned like this: #1 player is worth 60M #10 player is worth 40M #100 player is worth 20M Don't hold me for those figures, it's a bit more complex than that. data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:18780 | [2025-10-20 08:17] derbymanager : Development, on the other hand, depends on potential. Every player has "current power" (a calculation of how good he is right now in terms of skills) and a potential power that says how far can he grow. Potential is adjusted by club fit and the competition where he plays (team tier). No player will become a world class player while playing in 4th division. He needs to go to 1st division to become world class (assuming he has potential to even reach that far). Club fit is in there to make sure that potential isn't revealed simply by looking when someone started to complain about training.  Still, in a d4 team, a player with best potential will usually be able to grow more than the one with low potential. From manager's point of view, without metagaming, you would see a player grow and reach highest price in your team and he would ask to leave. You could then decide whether you want to sell him for the money or to keep him for his skills...

And tier + league define revenues, more or less. So we can treat these as static values. D4 teams get between on average X money, or at most Y money. Whatever we need. The X and Y are static since the beginning basically.  However, what's not static are players. Their values and demands are relative to their power (and a bunch of other modifiers but we can ignore these, the quality highly correlates to price). And, over time, the average quality of players increased. Training is too good (if I nerf it, people are unhappy), schools got improved (people were unhappy before), and just the general churn of shitty players makes it so that the average value of d4 team has increased significantly compared to the season 1 (or whichever older season you want to take as benchmark).  So, average player quality increased, and with that average demands have increased... but the finances are constant, as I mentioned earlier.  Giving more money to d4 teams is counter productive IMO. It leads towards inflation, while I wanted to anchor the system somehow so that I don't have to inflate every other financial thing in the game too. The fact that teams are having salary issues and struggling is because teams in d4 consist of bigger teams that have dropped down and teams that have maxed out their squads so it's hard to compete with a normal squad...

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part2.txt:5878 | [2019-12-10 23:16] derbymanager : 1.) Roles. Previously, players were fixed. They played in 1-3 roles and that was it. It is true that you could switch roles easier, assuming the player supported them. This is the reason why it takes a couple of days to switch player's role so that your opponent couldn't surprise you.  But the main reason I made the switch is because now I can easily add new roles to players (there are currently 75 combinations compared to 40 that were before) and it should make training directly connected to what happens on the field. I'll come back to training later but I wanted to connect training with the game instead of having just some add-on that improves price no matter what you choose.

There won't be exact number because that would turn the game into chasing that one number, but a number of indicators will be shown and it will be up to you to decide...

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part2.txt:7212 | [2020-01-30 07:09] saltylem0n_ : **Assistant manager** takes care of squad's physical skills and helps them recover from injuries faster. He gives up to +4% per star bonus to both injury recovery and training speed for physical skills (speed, strength, work rate and set pieces).  **Technical coach** is responsible for training technical skills of your players. He increases the training speed by up to +4% per star for technical skills: tackling, accuracy, passing, technique, finishing, handling.  **Tactical coach** handles the training of tactical skills. Like others, he also increases the training speed by up to +4% per star for: ball control, anticipation, positioning, vision, off the ball and marking skills.  **Business manager** handles finances and increases the revenue from sponsors. His effort depends on your facilities level and will bring up to 60000 money per star. Use business manager if you want stable and reliable income per day.  **Brand specialist** takes care of club's brand recognition. He increases home match attendance (up to 4000 per star) and merchandise revenue (up to 40000 per star), both of which depend on fans' satisfaction. If your fans are happy and your teamwork is high, you might want to consider using brand specialists instead of business managers. While merchandise income on itself is lower than sponsors, increased income from attendance can easily offset the total revenue in brand specialist's favour.  **Scout** can bring youth players into your club and help you identify scouting targets. He increases the potential and initial power of your youths and the rate at which your club generates them, all by up to 4% per star. He will also increase the rate at which you regenerate scout reports by the same amount and help you a bit to find potential transfer targets.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:540 | [2023-02-23 13:44] derbymanager : I decided because of a couple of reasons: - I always felt like seasons went by too fast in old DM. For me at least. Now two months is maybe a bit too long for my taste but I wanted to try it. I was thinking 1.5 months but that would make it complicated to track... - We will have transfer windows this time so there needs to be a couple of days free in the "winter" to make transfers. - I want to make the world more vivid. With 2 games per day it would feel cluttered I think. - Some people had trouble setting up their squads because their game was during the night or they were unavailable for those 6 hours between the first and second game... Now it'll be 1 game per day only and cca 24 hours to update. - I think there will be youth games in later versions so that'll be the 2nd game of the day to check out.  I think that's it.

First scout gives you insight on skills and basic info, second reveals a bit more but also establishes contact, giving you better terms in contract negotiations, and finally 3rd scout is publicly stating interest, at which point the news show up in everyone's timeline that you're interested. data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:592 | [2023-03-22 12:52] derbymanager : So, I can't decide on season length and I have to make that choice soon because other things depend on it...  Option 1: Season lasts 2 months, 1 game per day with some days having no games if you're out of cups. Periods after 28th in the month are without games. Option 2: Season lasts 6 weeks. There is a league game every day and cup games are approx. every second day in later times. Option 3: Season lasts 1 month. There are 2 games almost every day.  I was thinking of going with option 1 but when I created players' contracts and they lasted for 6 months it seemed too far in the future. I now cut contracts to 2 seasons only (4 months) but still it feels quite slow. Especially since there will be transfer windows, so you might sign a player beginning of March, he would join in April, and his contract would last until September... The good side of option 1 was to allow for youth teams and games in the evening hours but I'm uncertain if this is something that would be interesting to most people. They're basically just friendlies.  As I already said, option 3 with 1 month season seemed too short for me. It was squeezed tight and I think some people felt under pressure to sign in twice per day just to play. On the other hand, it created some nice history. We actually did manage to see 2-3 generations of players emerge from this schedule and there was always something happening... However, going this route would definitely mean cutting out youth matches, but I was thinking of implementing some kind of loaning system for youngsters perhaps. In this case I think there would be only one transfer window between seasons (no winter window). Definitely no youth teams as we had previously. Maybe B teams the way Barcelona and Real have them (teams that couldn't progress to 1st division)...  Finally, I was playing around with 6 weeks seasons (option 2). Two windows but no youth teams. The biggest problem here is not knowing when the next season starts (it's not 1st in the month).

Budget for first two should not have changed because the amount paid to players was doubled but so was the frequency of payments. So, only thing that should have changed was budget for transfer fees. data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:10930 | [2024-08-24 08:42] derbymanager : I agree that the game promotes and rewards us to play in this way but I don't think doubling down on the meta is the way to go. Different roles spending more condition is fair IMO, it forces you to have a long bench if you want to play high press formations. The fact that people feel the best approach is to have 11x 4 star players and 11x 1.5 star players instead of 16x 3 star players is what I want to change. I don't blame anyone for playing this way, I understand that we all react to the game. My job is to use mechanics to nudge you to react in a different way...  Reducing condition impact and injuries really promotes first 11 and nobody else approach. We had a problem in DM1 where people would take over a bot team with 22 players, sell 11 and buy 5 players that are twice as good. Sell the ones you didn't sell in the first batch and you now have 11 players that are twice as good. Fill up to a minimum requirement with shitty players with maybe 2 good reserves to cover for short injuries and cards. Longer injury? Just sell and buy new player who isn't injured...  There are some differences between DM1 and DM2 but I want to move away from that model. I want you to have 16 starters and 5 reserves/youngsters, and rotate them intelligently, aiming to have the best 541 squad for your match against City, and best 433 for your match against Wolves the next day. And I want the game to put obstacles in front of you to make it sometimes hard to achieve that (injuries, cards, condition are such obstacles, some you can't control, some you can)...

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:2711 | [2025-07-31 09:56] derbymanager : The game is changing pretty fast as it's still in beta while I try to balance it all... The best approach is to simply ask here on discord and people will help you out.  From the design perspective, the goal is to reward having a balanced team, a mixture of mentors, youth prospects and everything in between. Whenever there is a perceived meta I try to nerf it so that it isn't the best (or only) way to play. Even if one approach is perhaps too good at the moment, you can count on it getting worse in the future.  In terms of how to play, my suggestion would be: - Analyse your team, make sure you have good players all around for the formation you intend to play (it's enough to just look at the stars in the squad selection screen). Don't shy away from playing players out of position, they'll learn the new position and will play well there in 5-10 games. - Generally speaking, 1 or 2 bad players in your squad won't break you. You can play a formation that you know works well and fill a position or two with 500k youngster if needed. Of course, better players usually mean better results, but that's not guaranteed and prepare that you'll get angry at match engine occasionally 😬 - If you need money you can sell one good player and buy two ok ones. For example, you sell Valle and buy two 5-8M players to fill up your squad with 3.5 star players. You have a lot of youngsters, maybe offload those you don't intend to play and buy another 5-8M player. Selling shitty players might be tough, though. - Your main goal should be to go up to 3rd division. Don't worry about player development, facilities, or anything else. I would buy older (25+) quality players that will push you up. The rewards basically double with each division so you want to get as high as possible as fast as you can.
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:2713 | [2025-07-31 10:08] derbymanager : I realized I didn't answer almost any of your questions 😅   > Like what to do at the start - which players do I sell, which players are worth buying at the start? Try to have 15 players with 3-4 stars in your squad. Better to have a good average squad than few top players and the rest all shitty ones. > How does the yout school work, when to promote youths? For a season you can observe 4 players in youth school. After 3 weeks you'll see their potential and all skills. If you like them, you can hire them. If you don't, you can find a new player at any time. When they reach their training limit in the school there will be a message so you can promote them if you think they'll get some playtime in your squad.  > Are players who are reaching their peak at the club worth keeping or should I get rid of them? On the training screen you can see a yellow or red icon that the player is close to reaching their peak in your team. That means that they could still grow but would need a better team to do so. If you're about to get promoted it might be worth keeping them. Otherwise you might consider selling them and buying some that can grow or that won't be unhappy. Having a couple unhappy players is ok, having half of the team unhappy is problematic. There is no right or wrong way, assess your squad and decide. * > What is sharpness and how important is it? Sharpness is increased by playing games and it's pretty important but not so much to avoid playing a good player with low sharpness. It grows quickly and it's basically here to promote rotating your squad so that you'd have more than 11 players ready to play at all times. > How much do mentors really contribute to the training? Quite a lot. They boost your facilities. > If I got w low-division club am I stuck with it for a longer time and should prepare to build it or do I get offers from better teams relatively soon? You'll get offers from better teams when you go up into 3rd division and survive there.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:3238 | [2025-08-27 23:29] furysk : from recent experience as someone in IV who was 7-10-20 in their first 37 and 27-6-6 in the last 39, the things that made it work for me after a while:  1) Do not build to a formation that works for someone else.  they have the players to make it work, you probably dont, so just build your team based on what you have to work with early on.  The only formations that tend not to work as easily (though still doable) are ones that aren't somewhat symmetrical.  It takes some good studying to make them work, best to not go that route until you feel like you have a good understanding.  2) Do not chase guys with high potential unless your plan is to then spin said player.  Happiness once those players hit the maximum for the level will plummet, and you'll have volatile performances.  If you can buy a player for 1-1.5M and get them to grow a lot and sell them for 4.5-5M, then fair play, but the idea of having that guy be the cornerstone of the franchise isn't feasible unless your teams growth is really significant (meaning you are in tier 1 in 4-5 seasons)  3) Look at literally any player that can help you now.  Experience is great, but if you can find the right guy that is 22-25 and is near the end of development, make them your tier 4 cornerstone and hope they accept a backup contract down the road or they can be sold to be someone elses tier 4 winning player.  I only know of your MC/FC, as i listed him this season, you have a solid False Nine and a good attacking-minded midfielder there.  iirc I even made him work at holding mid, though that wasn't the ideal setup.  I can give you some thoughts in <#1102891926371438623> for what you have i guess in brief

In d4 you get 2M for winning the league, 4M in d3. Everything below that is proportionally lower.  So if you can buy a 2M player and you have two options: A.) 31yo that has skills at 12 B.) 21yo that has skills at 10  Let's say that with player A you'll finish 1st and with B you'll finish 4th. In reality I doubt 1 player can make such difference but let's assume the most extreme scenario. That's a difference of maybe 500k in d4, 1M in d3... Probably lower because the difference in money between 1st and 4th is bigger than between 11th and 14th.  Player A will lose some value in that season, so whatever you earn extra will be lower. Keep in mind that we already assumed huge impact of this single player on your final position. It's not unbelievable that any extra you earn is completely negated with this one old player.  There is also boost to your reputation and possibly higher earnings later on if you get promoted, but that only matters if with that old guy you get promotion and without him you don't, which probably isn't the case for most teams.  There's also passive training boost, but that makes that player lose even more value...  On the other hand if you go with player B, there is a chance that player will earn you those 500k or 1M simply from training. Even if he stagnates, he most likely won't lose value.  In addition, player B will be better next season while player A will be worse. If in first season player B got you +3 positions on the league table, in 2nd season it'll be +1 position, and third season  B player is better.  ---  Now do the same math with 5 players and the gap becomes bigger and bigger.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part5.txt:5495 | [2025-03-17 20:10] endgamenow : The point of the table was to see how teams would perform given they maximised their potential.  Teams use money to buy players. When they buy a player, they're investing money into that player hoping they'll improve in their value (in moneyball belief, which is what I believe most people in IT4 are thinking of).  Facilities help increase the worth of said player e.g. you buy a player for 2 million, facilities increase worth of that player by 1.5 million and hey you now have a player worth 3.5 million - and then you can sell that player and gain a 1.5 million return on investment. Opportunity cost is another discussion but right now we're talking solely about player value and wanting a higher return.  As you can see, facilities have acted as a means to increase the player's value and therefore there is a direct correlation when calculating the maximum potential of a team.  As stated before, the table is designed to project the long term - "for all we know the ENLP might be more accurate the season after this one if managers don't utilise all of their resources." which is why facilities have also been counted in.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part6.txt:9363 | [2025-01-01 21:02] derbymanager : So, to remove any confusion, there are several things at play here:  - Every position has certain popularity assigned. It works in such way that 12th in d2 is more popular than 1st in d3 (and similarly for other divisions). However, your team doesn't automatically get the popularity for its position. Instead, every Monday the popularity moves a certain percentage towards the popularity for that position. E.g. if popularity for your position is 12 but you are at 8, on Monday it will jump to 8.6 or whatever, I don't know exactly. So, it's unlikely your popularity drops with promotion (it could happen if your team went quickly down and then back up by a big margin or some similar edge case).  - After this popularity is calculated, all teams are sorted in order from most popular to least popular and a tier is assigned to them so that there are 20 teams in top tier, 50 in the next one etc... Same is done for players, best 200 players are top tier, next 1000 are next tier etc... This is what actually affects who are you able to buy. So, depending on which teams go up or down in popularity your tier can change even if your popularity stays the same. E.g. if your popularity is 8.6 and 10 teams with popularity 8.7 go down below 8.6, you would overtake them when it comes to team tier. This shouldn't make too much of a difference though since some other teams will overtake you and you'll always be pretty close to where you should be.  - Finally, there are also end of season bonuses in popularity for final standing as well as for cup(s) if you progressed a bit so going up a division will almost certainly improve your popularity/tier. As I said, I can imagine an edge case where that's not the case, but it vast majority of cases it should improve.
